questions.question: What is the mandatory action required when approaching an octagonal red STOP traffic sign?
questions.a: Slow down to 20 km/h and proceed if clear
questions.b: Come to a complete stop before the stop line or pedestrian lane and yield to all traffic
questions.c: Stop only if another motor vehicle is approaching from the right
questions.d: Honk your horn and proceed cautiously across the intersection
questions.explanation: Under DPWH & LTO regulations, an octagonal STOP sign requires a complete full stop at the stop line or pedestrian crossing, yielding the right of way to cross traffic.

questions.question: What does an inverted triangular sign with a red border (GIVE WAY / YIELD) signify to approaching drivers?
questions.a: Vehicles on the main road must yield to you
questions.b: You have priority over all intersecting roads
questions.c: Slow down and give way (yield) to vehicles on the major road or roundabout
questions.d: Mandatory full stop for at least 5 seconds
questions.explanation: The GIVE WAY (YIELD) sign instructs drivers to slow down and prepare to stop if necessary to yield the right-of-way to vehicles on the priority road.

questions.question: What does a circular white sign with a red outer border and a red diagonal slash over a black left arrow indicate?
questions.a: Compulsory left turn ahead
questions.b: No Left Turn permitted at this intersection
questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal slash is a prohibitory sign. Over a left arrow, it prohibits making any left turns.

questions.question: What is prohibited when encountering a red circle sign with a curved U-arrow and diagonal slash?
questions.a: No Left Turn
questions.explanation: The No U-Turn regulatory sign strictly prohibits drivers from reversing direction 180 degrees at the marked location.

questions.question: What does a solid red circular sign displaying a bold horizontal white bar indicate?
questions.a: No Parking
questions.c: NO ENTRY to all vehicular traffic
questions.explanation: The solid red disc with a horizontal white bar is the universal NO ENTRY sign prohibiting all vehicles from entering a one-way street or restricted zone.

questions.question: What does a circular sign showing a pedestrian symbol with a red diagonal slash mean?
questions.a: Pedestrians have right of way
questions.explanation: A pedestrian silhouette with a red diagonal slash indicates that pedestrians are prohibited from walking along or crossing this roadway (e.g. expressways).

questions.question: What does a circular white sign with a red border showing a bicycle with a red diagonal slash mean?
questions.a: Bicycles only lane
questions.b: Bicycles prohibited from using this road
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits bicycles, non-motorized pedal bikes, and e-bikes from entering expressways and designated high-speed thoroughfares.

questions.question: What does a circular white sign with a red border showing a motorcycle with a red diagonal slash indicate?
questions.a: Motorcycle parking only
questions.b: Motorcycles prohibited from entering this road section
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits all types of motorcycles and mopeds from entering specific tunnels, flyovers, or restricted roads.

questions.question: What does a circular white sign with a red border showing a motorized tricycle with a red diagonal slash indicate?
questions.a: Tricycles prohibited on this national highway or main road
questions.explanation: Under DILG & LTO directives, tricycles and pedicabs are strictly prohibited from operating along national highways.

questions.question: What does a circular sign with a red border showing a truck silhouette with a red diagonal slash mean?
questions.a: Truck scale station ahead
questions.c: Heavy trucks prohibited during designated hours or on this bridge/road
questions.explanation: This prohibitory sign bans cargo trucks and heavy vehicles from traversing urban streets or residential thoroughfares.

questions.question: What does a circular sign displaying '5t' inside a red circular border signify?
questions.a: Minimum weight allowed is 5 tonnes
questions.b: Maximum Gross Vehicle Weight (Gross Axle Load) limit is 5 tonnes
questions.explanation: Vehicles exceeding 5 metric tons in gross weight are strictly prohibited from crossing or using this bridge/road.

questions.question: What does a circular sign displaying '3.5m' between two vertical arrowheads pointing inward signify?
questions.a: Maximum vehicle height clearance limit is 3.5 meters
questions.b: Maximum vehicle width limit is 3.5 meters
questions.c: Distance to next exit is 3.5 km
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign indicates the maximum allowable vehicle height that can safely pass under an overpass or tunnel.

questions.question: What does a circular sign displaying '2.4m' between two horizontal arrowheads pointing inward signify?
questions.a: Minimum lane width is 2.4 meters
questions.b: Maximum vehicle width limit is 2.4 meters
questions.d: Distance between vehicles must be 2.4 meters
questions.explanation: Vehicles wider than 2.4 meters (including side mirrors/cargo) cannot enter due to physical lane narrowness.

questions.question: What does a circular sign with a red border and a straight right arrow with a diagonal slash mean?
questions.a: Right lane ending
questions.b: No Right Turn permitted at this intersection
questions.c: One way road to the right
questions.explanation: The No Right Turn sign strictly prohibits turning right at the marked junction.

questions.question: What does a circular white sign with a red border showing a horn with a red diagonal slash mean?
questions.a: Honk horn before proceeding
questions.b: Sounding of vehicle horn is strictly prohibited (Quiet / Hospital / School Zone)
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits unnecessary sounding of motor vehicle horns, typically near hospitals, schools, and courthouses.

questions.question: What does a circular regulatory sign with a black left arrow AND right arrow with a red slash mean?
questions.a: Proceed straight only (No Turns allowed)
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits both left and right turns, forcing all vehicles to continue straight ahead.

questions.question: What does a circular sign with a red border showing an animal-drawn cart with a red diagonal slash mean?
questions.a: Carabao crossing zone
questions.b: Animal-drawn carts (Kalesas / Kuligligs) are prohibited on this roadway
questions.explanation: Animal-drawn carriages and agricultural tractors are prohibited from main expressways and highways.

questions.question: What does a rectangular white sign with black text saying 'ONE WAY' accompanied by an arrow mean?
questions.a: Traffic moves exclusively in the direction of the arrow
questions.explanation: The ONE WAY sign dictates that all vehicular movement is restricted to a single uniform direction.

questions.question: What does a circular white sign with a red border showing '10m' between two cars indicate?
questions.a: Speed limit 10 km/h
questions.b: Minimum following distance of 10 meters must be maintained between moving vehicles
questions.explanation: This sign mandates maintaining a minimum spatial gap of at least 10 meters from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What does a white rectangular sign with a red circular border saying 'CUSTOMS' or 'PULIS' mandate?
questions.a: Speed up to clear checkpoint
questions.b: All drivers must stop for police or customs inspection before proceeding
questions.explanation: Drivers must stop completely at the inspection post and submit to authorized vehicle checks.

questions.question: What does a circular blue sign containing a straight white arrow pointing directly upward signify?
questions.a: One way street to the right
questions.explanation: Blue circular signs are mandatory regulatory signs. A vertical upward arrow indicates all vehicles must proceed straight ahead only; turning is not permitted.

questions.question: What does a circular blue sign with a white diagonal arrow pointing down and to the right instruct drivers to do?
questions.a: Keep Right of the traffic island or obstruction
questions.b: Right turn only at the next corner
questions.explanation: A blue circle with a downward-angled arrow is the mandatory KEEP RIGHT sign, directing traffic to pass to the right of a median island or divider.

questions.question: What does a circular sign depicting two cars side-by-side with a red diagonal slash prohibit?
questions.a: Drag racing on public roads
questions.explanation: The No Overtaking sign prohibits passing other vehicles on that section of the road due to limited sight distance, curves, or hazard areas.

questions.question: What is the meaning of a blue circular sign containing three curved white arrows in a clockwise circle?
questions.a: U-turn slot ahead
questions.explanation: This mandatory sign directs drivers to navigate the upcoming roundabout (rotonda) in the specified circular direction.

questions.question: What does a circular blue sign with a white arrow turning 90 degrees to the left mandate?
questions.a: Compulsory Left Turn ahead; all vehicles must turn left
questions.d: One way traffic to the right
questions.explanation: This mandatory sign instructs all drivers in this lane that they must turn left at the upcoming intersection.

questions.question: What does a circular blue sign with a white arrow turning 90 degrees to the right mandate?
questions.a: Compulsory Right Turn ahead; all vehicles must turn right
questions.explanation: This mandatory sign requires all vehicles to turn right at the intersection.

questions.question: What does a circular blue sign with a white bifurcated arrow pointing both Straight and Right indicate?
questions.a: Vehicles may either proceed straight or turn right
questions.explanation: This mandatory direction sign permits traffic in this designated lane to either continue straight or execute a right turn.

questions.question: What does a circular blue sign with a white bifurcated arrow pointing both Straight and Left indicate?
questions.a: Vehicles may either proceed straight or turn left
questions.explanation: Traffic in this lane is authorized to either proceed straight ahead or make a left turn.

questions.question: What does a circular blue sign with an arrow pointing down and to the left mean?
questions.a: Keep Left of the traffic divider or obstacle
questions.explanation: Mandatory KEEP LEFT sign instructing motorists to steer to the left side of the divider or traffic island.

questions.question: What does a circular blue sign showing white arrows pointing down to BOTH the left and right mean?
questions.a: Pass on either side of the traffic island or obstruction
questions.explanation: Vehicles are permitted to pass on either the left or right side of the physical roadway divider.

questions.question: What does a blue circular sign depicting a white bus silhouette indicate?
questions.a: Bus terminal ahead
questions.b: Mandatory Bus Lane / Public Utility Bus designated route
questions.explanation: This mandatory sign designates exclusive bus lanes (such as the EDSA Busway) for authorized public utility buses.

questions.question: What does a blue circular sign depicting a white bicycle silhouette indicate?
questions.a: Bicycle repair shop
questions.b: Mandatory Bicycle Lane (exclusive for bicycles and light personal mobility devices)
questions.explanation: Mandatory sign marking dedicated bicycle lanes where motorized cars and trucks are prohibited from driving or parking.

questions.question: What does a blue circular sign showing a white pedestrian silhouette signify?
questions.a: Pedestrian overpass only
questions.b: Compulsory Pedestrian Footpath / Walkway (Vehicles strictly prohibited)
questions.explanation: This mandatory sign marks a dedicated pedestrian pathway where all motorized vehicles are forbidden.

questions.question: What does a white circular sign with a red border showing a red diagonal line across a black truck passing a car mean?
questions.a: Trucks prohibited from overtaking other vehicles
questions.b: No trucks allowed on this road
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign prohibits heavy trucks from switching lanes to overtake other vehicles on multi-lane highways.

questions.question: What does a blue rectangular sign with a white 'P' and an arrow pointing to a curb bay indicate?
questions.a: Designated Parking Zone in the direction indicated
questions.explanation: Informative regulatory sign indicating an authorized area for motor vehicle parking.

questions.question: What does a circular blue sign showing '30' with a white border indicate?
questions.a: Maximum speed 30 km/h
questions.b: Compulsory Minimum Speed Limit of 30 km/h
questions.explanation: A number inside a solid blue circle is a Compulsory Minimum Speed Limit sign. Vehicles must not travel slower than 30 km/h under normal conditions.

questions.question: What does a white circular sign with a red border and diagonal slash over a car and motorcycle signify?
questions.a: All motor vehicles prohibited from entering
questions.explanation: This prohibitory sign bars all motorized vehicular traffic (cars, trucks, motorcycles) from entering a pedestrianized zone.

questions.question: What does a blue circular sign showing a white snow chain on a tire mean?
questions.a: Tire pressure check station
questions.b: Compulsory use of tire snow chains or traction devices (mountain passes in winter/mud)
questions.explanation: Mandatory sign requiring specialized tire traction devices on designated slippery mountain routes.

questions.question: What does a blue circular sign showing two white arrows facing each other vertically mean?
questions.a: Two-way traffic flow mandatory
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, this blue sign indicates you have priority over oncoming vehicles traveling in the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does a red circular sign showing a red arrow up and a black arrow down indicate?
questions.a: You must give way to oncoming traffic on this single-lane narrow section
questions.b: You have right of way over oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: A red circle showing a red forward arrow and black oncoming arrow requires you to yield to oncoming vehicles in narrow passages.

questions.question: What does a circular white sign with a red border containing the numeral '60' mean?
questions.a: Minimum required speed is 60 km/h
questions.b: Maximum legal speed limit is 60 km/h
questions.explanation: A number inside a red circle is the Maximum Speed Limit sign. You must not exceed 60 km/h under normal road conditions.

questions.question: What does a blue circular sign with a red border and a single diagonal red slash over the letter 'P' indicate?
questions.a: No Parking anytime
questions.explanation: The letter 'P' with a red slash indicates NO PARKING. Stopping temporarily to load/unload passengers for less than 1 minute without leaving the driver's seat may be allowed unless a No Stopping sign is posted.

questions.question: What does a blue circular sign with a red border and a red 'X' (two intersecting diagonal slashes) signify?
questions.a: No Overtaking
questions.b: No Stopping and No Standing at any time
questions.explanation: A red 'X' over a blue circular disc is the NO STOPPING / NO STANDING sign, prohibiting even brief stops to drop off or pick up passengers.

questions.question: According to RA 4136, what is the maximum allowable speed limit for passenger cars and motorcycles on open country roads with no blind corners?
questions.a: 40 km/h
questions.explanation: Under Article I, Section 35 of RA 4136, the speed limit for passenger cars and motorcycles on open country roads with no blind corners is 80 km/h.

questions.question: According to RA 4136, within how many meters of an intersection is parking strictly prohibited?
questions.a: 2 meters
questions.explanation: Under RA 4136 Section 46, no driver shall park a vehicle within six (6) meters of the intersection of curb lines.

questions.question: According to RA 4136, within how many meters of a fire hydrant is parking strictly prohibited?
questions.a: 1 meter
questions.explanation: Under RA 4136 Section 46, parking is strictly prohibited within four (4) meters of the driveway entrance to any fire station or within 4 meters of any fire hydrant.

questions.question: According to RA 4136, what is the maximum allowable speed limit for passenger cars on 'through streets' or boulevards clear of traffic?
questions.a: 30 km/h
questions.explanation: Under RA 4136 Section 35, the speed limit for passenger cars on through streets or boulevards with no blind corners is 40 km/h (30 km/h for heavy trucks and buses).

questions.question: Under RA 4136, what is the maximum legal speed limit for all motor vehicles on crowded city streets, intersections, and school zones?
questions.a: 20 km/h
questions.explanation: The statutory maximum speed limit on crowded streets, approaching intersections at blind corners, passing school zones, or passing stationary streetcars is 20 km/h.

questions.question: What does a rectangular sign with 'TOW-AWAY ZONE' placed underneath a No Parking sign indicate?
questions.a: Free towing service available for broken-down vehicles
questions.b: Any illegally parked vehicle will be clamped, towed, and impounded at the owner's expense
questions.d: No towing allowed on this road
questions.explanation: Vehicles violating parking restrictions in a designated Tow-Away Zone are immediately removed and subjected to heavy towing and storage fines.

questions.question: What does a circular white sign with a red border containing '80' crossed out by 4 diagonal gray slashes mean?
questions.a: Speed limit increases to 100 km/h
questions.b: End of 80 km/h speed limit restriction (Standard statutory road limits apply)
questions.explanation: The End of Speed Limit sign indicates the specific posted restriction has terminated and general traffic laws apply.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit for heavy trucks and buses on Philippine expressways (e.g. NLEX / SLEX)?
questions.a: 60 km/h
questions.explanation: Under expressway safety regulations and TRB rules, the maximum speed limit for heavy cargo trucks and public utility buses is 80 km/h.

questions.question: What does a 'NO LOADING AND UNLOADING ANYTIME' regulatory sign signify to public utility vehicle (PUV) drivers?
questions.a: PUVs may stop briefly for 30 seconds to drop passengers
questions.b: Stopping to let passengers board or alight or loading cargo is strictly prohibited under penalty of fine
questions.c: Only private cars may load passengers
questions.explanation: Strict prohibition against stopping for passenger boarding/alighting to prevent bottlenecks on critical road segments.

questions.question: Under RA 4136 Section 46, within how many meters of a railroad crossing is parking strictly prohibited?
questions.a: 4 meters
questions.explanation: Under RA 4136 Section 46(d), parking is prohibited within twelve (12) meters of the nearest rail of any railway crossing.

questions.question: What does a sign stating 'PARKING RESERVED FOR PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES (PWD)' indicate?
questions.a: Anyone may park if picking up groceries for a senior citizen
questions.b: Exclusive parking for vehicles displaying authorized PWD identification/stickers carrying a PWD passenger
questions.c: General public parking between 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM
questions.explanation: Under BP 344 (Accessibility Law) and traffic ordinances, unauthorized parking in designated PWD bays is punishable by law.

questions.question: What does a sign stating 'PARKING: 7:00 AM - 7:00 PM / NO PARKING: 7:01 PM - 6:59 AM' mean?
questions.a: Parking is permitted during daytime hours (7am to 7pm) and prohibited overnight
questions.d: Towing service operating during daytime only
questions.explanation: Time-regulated parking allows lawful parking only within the explicitly posted hours.

questions.question: What is the penalty under MMDA / LTO regulations for illegal parking on designated Mabuhay Lanes and national primary roads?
questions.a: ₱100 fine
questions.b: ₱1,000 fine for attended illegal parking, ₱2,000 for unattended illegal parking, plus towing fees
questions.d: Immediate suspension of vehicle registration for 10 years
questions.explanation: Fines for illegal parking on priority Mabuhay Lanes carry strict penalties and immediate towing for unattended vehicles.

questions.question: When parking a vehicle parallel to the curb on a level two-way street in the Philippines, your right-hand wheels must be within what distance of the curb?
questions.a: Within 30 centimeters (approx. 12 inches)
questions.explanation: Standard parallel parking regulations require parking within 30 cm of the curb to avoid impeding traffic flow.

questions.question: When parking a motor vehicle facing UPHILL on a street with a curb, which direction should you turn your front wheels?
questions.a: Straight ahead
questions.b: Turn wheels to the left (away from the curb) so the tire will roll back against the curb if brakes fail
questions.c: Turn wheels to the right (toward the curb)
questions.explanation: Turning wheels to the left away from the curb ensures that if the vehicle rolls backward, the front right tire will roll into and bind against the curb.

questions.question: When parking facing DOWNHILL on a street with a curb, which direction should you turn your front wheels?
questions.a: Turn wheels to the right (toward the curb) and engage handbrake and reverse gear
questions.d: Shift into neutral and release handbrake
questions.explanation: Turning wheels toward the curb ensures the front tire rolls directly into the curb if the vehicle begins creeping forward.

questions.question: Under RA 4136, is it lawful to leave a motor vehicle unattended on a highway with the engine running?
questions.a: Yes, if air conditioning is on
questions.b: No, the driver must turn off the engine, engage the parking brake, and remove the ignition key
questions.d: Yes, if hazard lights are flashing
questions.explanation: Under RA 4136 Section 47, no person shall leave a motor vehicle unattended without stopping the engine, locking the ignition, removing the key, and setting the handbrake.

questions.question: What does an equilateral triangular warning sign with an arrow curving to the left warn the driver about?
questions.a: Compulsory left turn ahead
questions.explanation: Triangular signs with red borders are Warning Signs. An arrow bending left warns of a sharp left curve ahead requiring speed reduction.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign with an arrow curving to the right indicate?
questions.a: Sharp right curve / bend ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of a sharp curve to the right ahead, requiring motorists to slow down before entering the curve.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a reverse double curve (zigzag arrow turning left then right) signify?
questions.a: Reverse Curve ahead (first to the left, then to the right)
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers of a reverse curve ahead where the road bends first to the left and then closely to the right.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a reverse double curve turning first to the right then to the left signify?
questions.a: Reverse Curve ahead (first to the right, then to the left)
questions.explanation: Warns of double bends where the road curves first to the right and subsequently to the left.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing an arrow that loops back 180 degrees to the left (Hairpin Bend) indicate?
questions.a: U-turn slot ahead
questions.b: Hairpin curve to the left (extremely sharp 180° bend) ahead
questions.explanation: The Hairpin Curve sign warns of an exceptionally sharp turn (common on mountain roads) requiring substantial braking and gear downshifting.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing a Hairpin Bend looping back 180 degrees to the right indicate?
questions.a: Hairpin curve to the right ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of an extreme 180-degree hairpin turn to the right ahead.

questions.question: What does a triangular sign showing a serpentine winding road symbol advise drivers to do?
questions.a: Expect a series of continuous winding curves ahead
questions.b: Watch out for crossing reptiles and wildlife
questions.explanation: The Winding Road sign warns of a series of three or more consecutive curves ahead, advising drivers not to overtake and to reduce driving speed.

questions.question: When driving around sharp curves on two-lane mountain roads in the Philippines, which practice is essential?
questions.a: Overtake slow trucks before entering the curve
questions.b: Stay strictly in your lane, sound your horn near blind curves, and do not cross the center line
questions.c: Shift to neutral gear to conserve fuel
questions.d: Turn on hazard warning flashers while driving at high speed
questions.explanation: On blind mountain curves, crossing the center line or overtaking is extremely hazardous. Stay in your lane and sound your horn during daytime to alert oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What do rectangular black-and-white (or yellow-and-black) Chevron alignment signs positioned around the outside of a sharp bend indicate?
questions.a: The sharp edge and directional flow of the curve requiring continuous steering guidance
questions.explanation: Chevron alignment markers guide the driver's visual path around hazardous sharp bends.

questions.question: What dangerous centrifugal effect occurs when a vehicle enters a curve at excessive speed?
questions.a: Understeer or rollover as inertia pushes the vehicle outwards away from the curve
questions.explanation: Excess speed around bends creates centrifugal forces that overcome tire friction, causing dangerous outward skidding (understeer) or rollovers.

questions.question: What is the proper technique for braking when negotiating a sharp highway curve?
questions.a: Brake firmly while in the middle of the turn
questions.b: Brake and reduce speed in a straight line BEFORE entering the curve, then gently accelerate through the apex
questions.c: Never use brakes; pull the handbrake instead
questions.d: Accelerate heavily into the entrance of the bend
questions.explanation: Braking mid-corner destabilizes vehicle balance and can trigger a spin. Always complete braking before turning the steering wheel.

questions.question: Why should drivers NOT depress the clutch pedal or coast in Neutral while navigating mountain curves?
questions.a: It disconnects engine braking, leaving the vehicle entirely reliant on friction brakes which can overheat and fade
questions.d: It causes transmission fluid to freeze
questions.explanation: Coasting in neutral robs you of engine resistance, causing runaway acceleration on downhill curves and severe brake fade.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign with a right-angle (90-degree) sharp bend symbol signify?
questions.a: Sharp right-angle turn ahead requiring almost complete deceleration
questions.explanation: Warns of a sudden 90-degree sharp bend that cannot be negotiated at standard cruising speeds.

questions.question: What does an advisory speed plate (e.g. '30 km/h') mounted directly below a curve warning sign mean?
questions.a: Mandatory minimum speed
questions.b: Recommended safe maximum speed for negotiating that specific curve under dry conditions
questions.explanation: Advisory speed plates provide recommended safe speeds specifically calibrated for that curve's geometry.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they encounter gravel or sand scattered across a sharp curve?
questions.a: Slam the brakes immediately
questions.b: Slow down gently before the patch, hold a steady steering angle, and avoid sudden throttle or braking inputs
questions.c: Accelerate rapidly to jump over the gravel
questions.d: Turn the steering wheel back and forth rapidly
questions.explanation: Loose gravel drastically reduces tire friction. Sudden steering or braking inputs will cause total loss of lateral grip.

questions.question: What does a triangular sign showing a car skidding with wavy tire marks mean?
questions.a: Slippery road surface ahead (especially when wet or muddy)
questions.explanation: Warns that road surface has low friction coefficient and becomes exceptionally slick during rain or oil spills.

questions.question: Why is the road surface most slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of light rainfall?
questions.a: Rainwater mixes with accumulated engine oil, grease, and road grime to form a slick emulsion before being washed away
questions.explanation: The initial minutes of rain loosen surface oils into a greasy film before heavy downpours can wash the residue away.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a car driving off a quay or riverbank into water indicate?
questions.a: Opening bridge ahead
questions.b: Unprotected riverbank, canal, or quayside ahead
questions.explanation: Warns that the road terminates at or runs adjacent to open water without protective barrier walls.

questions.question: When approaching a blind curve where visibility is restricted by rock faces or foliage, at what distance should you anticipate oncoming hazards?
questions.a: Only when you see their headlights 5 meters away
questions.b: Assume an oncoming vehicle may be encroaching on your lane and position yourself toward the outer right edge of your lane
questions.explanation: Defensive driving dictates hugging the safe right portion of your lane on blind curves to avoid head-on collisions.

questions.question: What should you do if an oncoming vehicle crosses the center line and drifts into your lane on a curve?
questions.a: Flash high beams, honk horn, brake smoothly, and steer toward the right shoulder/escape path
questions.explanation: Always evade to the right shoulder to prevent a catastrophic head-on crash.

questions.question: What does a triangular sign displaying a bold black plus symbol (+) warn of?
questions.a: Hospital or first aid station ahead
questions.explanation: A black cross inside a triangular warning sign warns drivers of a 4-way crossroad intersection ahead, requiring vigilance for crossing vehicles.

questions.a: T-Junction ahead where the road terminates and you must turn left or right

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers on a major road that side traffic is merging from the right ramp/side street ahead at an angle.

questions.question: When entering a multi-lane roundabout (rotonda) in the Philippines, which vehicle has the primary right-of-way?
questions.a: The vehicle entering the roundabout at highest speed
questions.b: Vehicles already navigating inside the circulatory roadway
questions.c: Public utility jeepneys and buses regardless of position
questions.d: The vehicle approaching from the leftmost entry lane
questions.explanation: Under standard Philippine traffic law and international conventions, vehicles already inside the roundabout circulatory roadway have right-of-way over vehicles entering.

questions.question: What does a triangular sign showing a vertical line with a perpendicular side road entering from the right indicate?
questions.a: Side road intersection on the right ahead
questions.d: One way road to the right
questions.explanation: Warns drivers that vehicles may enter or turn from a side road joining on the right.

questions.question: What does a triangular sign showing a vertical line with a perpendicular side road entering from the left indicate?
questions.a: Side road intersection on the left ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of a side junction on the left where vehicles may turn into or emerge onto the main thoroughfare.

questions.question: What does a triangular sign showing two staggered side roads (one left, then one right closely following) warn of?
questions.a: Staggered side road junctions ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of two closely spaced consecutive side junctions occurring on opposite sides of the main highway.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign with three arrows forming a circle (Roundabout Warning) indicate?
questions.a: Roundabout / Rotonda junction ahead; prepare to yield to circulating traffic
questions.explanation: Warns of an approaching circular intersection where traffic flows counter-clockwise and entry requires yielding.

questions.question: When planning to take the first exit (turning right) at a multi-lane roundabout, which lane should you approach and enter from?
questions.a: The leftmost lane
questions.b: The rightmost lane, signaling right as you approach and navigate
questions.explanation: To take the first exit to the right, enter in the right-hand lane and keep to the outer circulatory lane with your right turn signal on.

questions.question: When planning to take the third exit (turning left or making a 3/4 loop) at a roundabout, which lane should you enter from?
questions.a: The rightmost lane
questions.b: The leftmost (inner) lane, signaling left on entry and right before your intended exit
questions.explanation: For left turns or 270-degree loops in a roundabout, enter from the inside left lane, moving to the outside only after passing the exit preceding yours.

questions.question: What does a triangular sign showing an arrow pointing straight with a side ramp merging from the left indicate?
questions.a: Merging traffic from the left side ahead
questions.explanation: Warns that traffic from an on-ramp or side street will merge into the main stream from the left.

questions.question: What should a driver on an expressway acceleration lane do when preparing to merge onto the main highway?
questions.a: Stop dead at the start of the acceleration lane
questions.b: Match the cruising speed of expressway traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and merge smoothly into an open gap
questions.c: Honk loudly and force expressway cars to brake
questions.d: Drive across all lanes directly into the fast lane
questions.explanation: Acceleration lanes allow you to attain highway cruising speed so you merge seamlessly without interrupting moving traffic.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting two parallel lines with an obstruction starting in the middle indicate?
questions.a: Dual Carriageway (Divided Highway) Begins ahead
questions.explanation: Warns that the undivided two-way road will divide ahead into a dual carriageway separated by a physical median island.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a median island ending and traffic flowing onto a single undivided road indicate?
questions.a: Dual Carriageway (Divided Highway) Ends ahead; two-way traffic resumes
questions.explanation: Warns drivers that the physical median is ending and oncoming opposing traffic will share the continuous pavement.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing two vertical arrows pointing in opposite directions indicate?
questions.a: Two-Way Traffic flow ahead on the same roadway
questions.explanation: Warns drivers leaving a one-way street or divided section that opposing oncoming vehicles will now be present on the same carriageway.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing two horizontal arrows pointing in opposite directions across a road indicate?
questions.a: Two-way cross traffic ahead at the upcoming junction
questions.explanation: Warns that cross traffic on the intersecting street moves in both directions.

questions.question: What is the primary danger when approaching an uncontrolled intersection (an intersection without signals or stop signs)?
questions.a: Traffic lights are changing too quickly
questions.b: Cross traffic may enter the intersection without slowing down or yielding
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled junctions lack automated signals, requiring extreme defensive caution and covering the brake pedal.

questions.question: What does 'covering the brake' mean when approaching a busy intersection?
questions.a: Pressing the brake pedal with maximum force
questions.b: Hovering your right foot directly over the brake pedal without depressing it, ready for immediate reaction
questions.explanation: Covering the brake eliminates reaction delay (perception-to-foot movement), shaving critical meters off stopping distance in emergencies.

questions.question: Under standard defensive driving guidelines, if an intersection is congested and your vehicle cannot cross completely without stopping inside it, what must you do?
questions.a: Enter the intersection anyway and wait in the middle
questions.b: Wait behind the stop line until there is sufficient clear space on the other side to completely exit the junction
questions.explanation: Entering an intersection when the exit is blocked causes 'box blocking' and paralyzes cross traffic.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting road lines narrowing inward from both sides warn about?
questions.a: Road Narrows ahead on both sides
questions.explanation: The Road Narrows sign warns that the width of the carriageway is reducing from both sides, requiring drivers to merge smoothly and reduce speed.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.a: Road Narrows on the Left side ahead (left lane ends)
questions.explanation: Warns that the left lane or carriageway shoulder is tapering inward, requiring vehicles on the left to merge right.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a road narrowing on the Right side only mean?
questions.a: Road Narrows on the Right side ahead (right lane ends)
questions.explanation: Warns that the right side of the carriageway narrows, requiring right-lane traffic to merge smoothly to the left.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a car silhouette driving down a steep slope with a percentage (e.g. '10%') indicate?
questions.a: Steep Hill Descent (downhill slope) ahead
questions.explanation: The Steep Descent sign warns of a dangerous downward slope ahead. Drivers should shift to a lower gear to use engine braking and avoid brake fade.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.a: Steep Hill Ascent (uphill slope) ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of a steep upward climb ahead where vehicles may lose momentum and require downshifting.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting two curved humps in the road surface warn drivers of?
questions.a: Uneven or Bumpy Road surface ahead
questions.explanation: The Uneven Road sign warns of bumps, dips, or irregular road surface ahead that could compromise vehicle stability at higher speeds.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a single raised convex hump in the road surface indicate?
questions.a: Speed Hump / Speed Table ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of an artificial raised speed control hump designed to enforce low speeds in residential or pedestrian areas.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a concave depression or dip in the road surface warn of?
questions.a: Dip / Low Ground (Canal crossing or floodway dip) ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of a sudden downward dip in the road profile where vehicles traveling fast can bottom out or scrape bumpers.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting rocks falling down a slope warn motorists about?
questions.a: Falling or Fallen Rocks hazard ahead
questions.explanation: The Falling Rocks sign warns that landslides or rockfalls may occur on that mountain section, and debris may be obstructing the lane.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What dangerous phenomenon occurs when tires ride on a thin film of water rather than contacting the road surface during heavy rain?
questions.a: Engine vapor lock
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when water builds up under tires faster than tire treads can channel it away, causing total loss of steering and braking control.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What should you do immediately if your vehicle begins to hydroplane on standing water?
questions.a: Slam on the brakes and jerk the steering wheel
questions.b: Ease your foot off the accelerator smoothly, keep steering straight, and do not brake until tires regain asphalt contact
questions.explanation: Abrupt braking or turning while hydroplaning induces severe skidding. Allow deceleration to let tires sink through water film.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a Narrow Bridge indicate?
questions.a: Narrow Bridge ahead where road width contracts (may require alternating one-way passage)
questions.explanation: Warns that the upcoming bridge is narrower than the approaching carriageway.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting an Opening or Drawbridge indicate?
questions.a: Opening / Movable Drawbridge ahead; prepare to stop if red signals or barrier gates activate
questions.explanation: Warns that the bridge spans navigable waters and can be raised, halting all vehicular road traffic.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting loose stones / gravel flying from tires indicate?
questions.a: Loose Gravel or Chippings on road surface ahead; reduce speed and increase following distance
questions.explanation: Warns that newly surfaced gravel can fly up and shatter windshields or cause sudden loss of motorcycle traction.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing a person digging with a shovel warn of?
questions.a: Road Works / Construction / Maintenance ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of road crews, machinery, open trenches, or altered lane alignments ahead requiring reduced speed.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a low-flying airplane silhouette warn of?
questions.a: Airport runway nearby with Low-Flying Aircraft, sudden loud jet noise, and crosswinds
questions.explanation: Warns motorists driving adjacent to airport runways of startling aircraft noise and low flight paths.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing a windsock silhouette indicate?
questions.a: Severe Crosswinds / Strong Gusts hazard (open bridges, coastal causeways, mountain gaps)
questions.explanation: Warns of sudden lateral wind gusts that can destabilize high-profile vans, trucks, and motorcycles.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign displaying a large black exclamation point (!) warn of?
questions.a: General Danger / Unspecified Hazard ahead; proceed with heightened caution
questions.explanation: Warns of hazard conditions not covered by standard pictorial symbols, usually accompanied by an explanatory sub-plate.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a vehicle driving on a soft or sunken shoulder warn of?
questions.a: Soft / Unstabilized Verge or Low Road Shoulder ahead; avoid driving onto edges
questions.explanation: Warns that road edges lack firm foundation and dropping a wheel off the asphalt may cause rollovers or entrapment.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: When driving through deep floodwaters in the Philippines, what is the correct defensive driving technique?
questions.a: Drive through at 60 km/h to splash the water away
questions.b: Check water depth first; drive slowly in low gear maintaining steady engine RPM to prevent water entering the tailpipe, then test brakes after exiting
questions.d: Follow immediately behind a submerged motorcycle
questions.explanation: Driving slowly in first gear prevents creating a bow wave that drowns the intake and keeps exhaust pressure positive.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Road Width, Hills & Physical Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing a person walking between zebra crossing stripes indicate?
questions.a: Pedestrian Crossing (Zebra Crosswalk) ahead; yield to crossing pedestrians
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a marked pedestrian crossing is ahead. Drivers must slow down and yield right-of-way to any pedestrian stepping onto the zebra stripes.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a fluorescent yellow-green pentagonal (5-sided) or triangular sign showing two school children walking warn of?
questions.a: School Zone or Children Crossing ahead; reduce speed to 20 km/h
questions.explanation: The School Zone sign warns of school grounds or children crossing nearby. Drivers must observe school zone speed limits (maximum 20 km/h under RA 4136).
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does an 'X' shaped white crossbuck sign with the words 'RAILROAD CROSSING' require drivers to do?
questions.a: Speed up to cross the tracks before the train arrives
questions.b: Slow down, look both ways, listen for train horns, and stop if a train is approaching
questions.c: Stop only if a barrier gate is closed
questions.explanation: A Railroad Crossing Crossbuck sign marks a railway track crossing. Drivers must look and listen in both directions and come to a complete stop if signals flash or a train approaches.

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting an animal silhouette (e.g. cow or deer) indicate?
questions.a: Livestock / Animal Crossing zone ahead
questions.explanation: The Animal Crossing sign warns of areas where farm animals or wildlife may wander onto the roadway, particularly in rural provincial highways.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: When approaching a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm in the Philippines, you must:
questions.a: Overtake quickly on the left shoulder
questions.b: Come to a complete stop until the lights stop flashing and children have safely crossed
questions.c: Sound your horn repeatedly and drive past at 30 km/h
questions.d: Slow down only if driving a heavy truck
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights on a school bus mean children are boarding or disembarking. Traffic in both directions on undivided roads must stop completely.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a person in a wheelchair warn of?
questions.a: Persons with Disabilities (PWD) crossing area ahead; yield right of way
questions.explanation: Warns motorists to expect wheelchair users or mobility-impaired individuals crossing or using sidewalk curb cuts.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a bicycle indicate?
questions.a: Bicycle Crossing ahead; watch for cyclists entering from paths or shoulders
questions.explanation: Warns that cyclists frequently cross or merge with motor traffic at this location.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing an old-style steam locomotive warn of?
questions.a: Railroad Crossing WITHOUT automatic gates or barrier protection (Uncontrolled Railway)
questions.explanation: Warns that the railway track crossing lacks mechanical barrier arms, requiring extra driver vigilance before crossing.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing a railway track with a fence / gate barrier warn of?
questions.a: Railroad Crossing WITH automatic barrier gates or signals ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of a protected railway crossing equipped with drop-down barrier gates.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a rectangular white sign with red diagonal stripes (Counting Markers) before a railroad crossing indicate?
questions.a: Distance to railway tracks (e.g. 3 stripes = 150m, 2 stripes = 100m, 1 stripe = 50m)
questions.explanation: Distance countdown markers give drivers progressive warning as they approach a railway crossing.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing a car with headlights turned on with glare beams indicate?
questions.a: Low visibility / Fog-prone area ahead; turn on low-beam headlights or fog lights
questions.explanation: Warns of mountain fog, smoke, or coastal mist where driving visibility suddenly drops.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting horses or equestrian riders indicate?
questions.a: Horseback riders / Horse-drawn carriage crossing ahead; pass slowly and do not honk
questions.explanation: Warns of horses on the road. Loud horns must not be sounded to avoid spooking horses into traffic.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: When passing pedestrians walking along a rural road without sidewalks, what is the safest practice?
questions.a: Pass within 10 centimeters to save lane space
questions.b: Reduce speed, give at least 1 to 1.5 meters of lateral clearance, and be prepared for sudden movements
questions.c: Honk continuously until they jump into the ditch
questions.explanation: Pedestrians on unpaved shoulders require ample lateral safety buffer and reduced passing speed.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: Under Philippine traffic regulations, what must you do when approaching a pedestrian holding a white cane or accompanied by a guide dog?
questions.a: Sound your horn to tell them to move faster
questions.b: Come to a complete stop and yield absolute right-of-way, recognizing they are visually impaired
questions.c: Drive around them on the sidewalk
questions.d: Ignore them if the green light is on
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog signifies a blind pedestrian. Drivers must yield total priority regardless of traffic light status.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: Why is driving through a School Zone during morning opening (7:00 AM) and afternoon dismissal (4:00 PM) particularly hazardous?
questions.a: Children have limited peripheral vision, poor distance estimation, and may dart into traffic unpredictably between parked cars
questions.explanation: Young children lack mature traffic hazard perception and frequently cross without looking.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign depicting a blind or elderly pedestrian with a walking cane signify?
questions.a: Elderly / Frail Pedestrians crossing zone ahead (near nursing homes or senior centers)
questions.explanation: Warns drivers to expect slow-moving senior citizens who may require extra time to cross the road.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular sign showing a traffic light signal (Red, Yellow, Green) inside the triangle warn of?
questions.a: Traffic Signals ahead (Signalized intersection coming up around curve or over hill)
questions.explanation: Warns drivers of an approaching automated traffic light, particularly when sightlines are blocked by curves or topography.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a triangular warning sign showing a tractor / agricultural vehicle silhouette mean?
questions.a: Slow-moving Agricultural Farm Machinery entering or crossing highway ahead
questions.explanation: Warns of heavy, slow tractors, harvesters, and threshers entering provincial highways.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: If a ball bounces into the street from between parked cars in a residential neighborhood, what should you immediately anticipate?
questions.a: A dog chasing the ball
questions.b: A young child will likely run into the street immediately following the ball; slow down and prepare to stop instantly
questions.c: The ball will puncture your tire
questions.d: It is a prank; speed up
questions.explanation: Classic defensive driving rule: where a bouncing ball appears, a running child is almost guaranteed to follow.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: When driving past a public playground or park on a weekend, what is the recommended speed and mindset?
questions.a: Maintain maximum highway speed
questions.b: Reduce speed well below 20 km/h, cover the brake pedal, and scan between all parked vehicles
questions.explanation: High density of children near parks requires anticipatory brake covering and slow speed.
questions.moduleName: Warning Signs: Pedestrians, Schools & Special Hazards

questions.question: What does a Single Solid White center line on a two-lane road indicate?
questions.a: Overtaking is permitted anytime
questions.b: Separates traffic moving in opposite directions; crossing or overtaking is discouraged/prohibited
questions.explanation: A solid white line indicates that lane changing or crossing into opposing traffic is hazardous and discouraged, commonly used near junctions or blind spots.

questions.question: What does a Single Broken White center line on a multi-lane or two-way road mean?
questions.a: Lane changing and overtaking are permitted when safe to do so
questions.explanation: A broken white line separates lanes moving in the same direction or opposite directions where overtaking/lane switching is permitted when safe.

questions.question: What does a Double Solid Yellow line painted along the center of the road strictly mean?
questions.a: Overtaking is strictly prohibited for vehicles traveling in both directions
questions.b: Overtaking is permitted only during daytime
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean absolute prohibition of passing or crossing from either side under any circumstances.

questions.question: What does a combination of a Solid Yellow line with an adjacent Broken Yellow line mean?
questions.a: Only traffic on the side of the broken line may overtake when safe
questions.explanation: Vehicles traveling adjacent to the broken line may cross to overtake when clear, while traffic on the solid line side is strictly prohibited from passing.

questions.question: What does a Yellow Box painted with crisscross diagonal lines at an intersection mean?
questions.a: Do not enter the box unless your exit road is clear (No blocking the intersection)
questions.explanation: A Yellow Box Junction must never be blocked. Drivers must not enter the box unless their exit on the other side is completely clear to prevent gridlock.

questions.question: What does a solid white transverse line painted completely across your lane at an intersection represent?
questions.a: Stop Line where vehicles must come to a complete stop before crossing or when red signal appears
questions.explanation: The Stop Line defines the exact boundary behind which vehicles must stop at red lights, stop signs, or enforcer commands.

questions.question: What does a broken transverse white line (Give-Way Line) painted across a lane at an intersection or roundabout entry mean?
questions.a: Yield line where vehicles must slow down or stop to give way to intersecting or circulatory traffic
questions.explanation: Give-way lines mark where drivers must yield right-of-way before entering the priority thoroughfare.

questions.question: What do Zebra Pavement Stripes (broad alternating white longitudinal bars) painted across the street designate?
questions.a: Zebra Pedestrian Crosswalk where pedestrians have absolute right-of-way when crossing
questions.explanation: Zebra crossings are designated pedestrian zones where motor vehicles must yield completely to anyone on foot.

questions.question: What does a series of diagonal white or yellow hatched lines inside a solid border (Painted Traffic Island / Gore Area) mean?
questions.a: Prohibited chevron island; driving, parking, or crossing over this area is strictly illegal
questions.explanation: Painted islands separate diverging or converging traffic streams. Driving across chevron hatching is a moving violation.

questions.question: What does a Solid White Edge Line painted along the right outer edge of a highway delineate?
questions.a: The outer boundary of the drivable lane, separating it from the road shoulder or curb
questions.explanation: Edge lines (fog lines) help drivers orient lane position at night or in foggy conditions.

questions.question: What does a series of transverse raised rumble strips painted across the roadway produce when driven over?
questions.a: Auditory rumble noise and tactile vibration through tires to alert drivers to reduce speed before a toll plaza, hazard, or sharp bend
questions.explanation: Rumble strips physically and audibly warn fatigued or speeding motorists of approaching hazardous road conditions.

questions.question: What does a straight white arrow painted on the pavement inside a specific traffic lane instruct drivers to do?
questions.a: Traffic in that lane must proceed Straight ahead only
questions.c: Turn right at the next corner
questions.explanation: Pavement lane arrows dictate mandatory direction of travel for vehicles within that lane.

questions.question: What does a curved white arrow pointing left painted in a lane indicate?
questions.a: Dedicated Left Turn Lane only
questions.explanation: Vehicles positioned in this lane must execute a left turn at the intersection.

questions.question: What does a combination arrow showing both Straight and Left painted on the asphalt mean?
questions.a: Lane allows either proceeding straight ahead or making a left turn
questions.explanation: Permits both straight travel and left-turn maneuvers from this lane.

questions.question: What is a 'Motorcycle Lane' designated by blue or green pavement markings on major urban highways (e.g. Commonwealth Avenue / EDSA)?
questions.a: Dedicated/non-exclusive lane for motorcycles to organize traffic flow and prevent swerving
questions.explanation: Designated motorcycle lanes separate two-wheeled vehicles to curb reckless swerving across lanes.

questions.question: What does a Red painted curb along a city street signify?
questions.a: No Parking and No Stopping at any time (Fire lane or critical safety clearance)
questions.explanation: Red curbs denote critical emergency clearance zones where stopping is strictly prohibited.

questions.question: What does a Yellow painted curb along a street signify?
questions.a: No Parking (loading/unloading of commercial cargo may be permitted for designated brief periods)
questions.explanation: Yellow curbs indicate loading/unloading restrictions with general parking prohibited.

questions.question: What does a White painted curb indicate in urban street parking?
questions.a: Short-term parking or passenger passenger drop-off/pickup only (e.g. 5-minute limit)
questions.explanation: White curbs are designated for brief passenger loading and unloading.

questions.question: What does a Green painted curb indicate?
questions.a: Short-term limited time parking (usually 15 to 30 minutes during business hours)
questions.explanation: Green curbs designate short-duration parking for quick errands during posted hours.

questions.question: What do cat's eyes (Raised Reflective Pavement Markers - RRPMs) in red color along the road edge indicate?
questions.a: The road shoulder or off-limits edge line (Do not cross to the left of red reflectors)
questions.explanation: Red reflectors mark the boundary edge of the road; driving outside them puts you on the road shoulder or verge.

questions.question: What does a Steady Red traffic light signal require drivers to do?
questions.a: Come to a complete stop before the stop line and remain stopped until green appears
questions.b: Proceed cautiously if no police officer is present
questions.d: Slow down to 10 km/h and cross if intersection is empty
questions.explanation: A steady red light mandates a complete stop before the stop line or pedestrian lane until a green signal or authorized green turn arrow appears.

questions.question: What is the meaning of a Flashing Yellow traffic light at an intersection?
questions.a: Prepare to stop completely immediately
questions.b: Slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection, yielding to cross traffic if necessary
questions.c: Traffic light is defective; speed up to clear intersection
questions.d: Pedestrians are not allowed to cross
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light serves as a warning signal. Motorists should reduce speed and proceed through the junction with heightened caution.

questions.question: What does a Flashing Red traffic light signal indicate?
questions.a: Equivalent to a STOP sign: come to a full complete stop, yield to cross traffic, then proceed when clear
questions.explanation: A flashing red light operates identically to an octagonal STOP sign: you must make a complete stop before the crosswalk, yielding to all cross traffic before proceeding.

questions.question: When a traffic enforcer is manually directing traffic and their signal conflicts with a green traffic light, which instruction must you follow?
questions.a: Always follow the traffic enforcer's manual hand signals over the electric traffic light
questions.b: Follow the electric traffic light at all times
questions.c: Honk your horn and wait until both signals match
questions.d: Follow the action of the car directly ahead of you
questions.explanation: Under RA 4136 and LTO regulations, manual instructions from an authorized traffic enforcer or police officer supersede and override all automated traffic lights and road signs.

questions.question: What is the proper hand signal for making a Left Turn when your electric turn signals are inoperative?
questions.a: Extend left arm and hand horizontally straight out of the window
questions.b: Extend left arm pointing upward at a 90-degree angle
questions.c: Extend left arm pointing downward at a 90-degree angle
questions.d: Wave left hand rapidly in a circular motion
questions.explanation: To signal a left turn manually, extend the left arm horizontally straight out from the driver's side window.

questions.question: What is the proper manual hand signal for making a Right Turn out of the driver's window?
questions.a: Extend left arm out and bend the elbow upward at a 90-degree angle with hand pointing toward the sky
questions.c: Point index finger to the right inside the car
questions.explanation: Right turn manual signal: Left arm out the window, elbow bent 90 degrees upward with palm facing forward.

questions.question: What is the proper manual hand signal for Stopping or Slowing Down?
questions.a: Extend left arm out the window pointing downward at a 90-degree angle with palm facing the rear
questions.explanation: Stop / Slow Down signal: Left arm extended downward at a 90-degree angle with palm toward approaching rear traffic.

questions.question: What does a Steady Yellow (Amber) traffic light signal mean as you approach an intersection?
questions.a: Speed up to beat the red light
questions.b: The signal is about to turn red; stop safely before the stop line unless you are so close that stopping abruptly would cause a rear-end collision
questions.explanation: Yellow light indicates caution: stop if safe to do so. Accelerating to beat a yellow is an aggressive and dangerous violation.

questions.question: What does a Steady Green traffic light signal permit you to do?
questions.a: Proceed straight ahead or make lawful turns, provided the intersection is clear and pedestrians have finished crossing
questions.b: Accelerate with maximum power without looking
questions.c: Make a U-turn even if a No U-turn sign is posted
questions.d: Block the intersection if traffic is stalled
questions.explanation: Green light permits moving straight or turning subject to yielding to pedestrians already in the crosswalk.

questions.question: What does a Green Arrow traffic signal pointing to the right indicate?
questions.a: Vehicles in the right-turn lane have a protected right turn and may proceed regardless of the main circular red light
questions.b: Stop and wait for the green circle
questions.explanation: A green arrow grants exclusive, protected right-of-way to make the indicated turn.

questions.question: What does a Green Arrow traffic signal pointing to the left indicate?
questions.a: Protected Left Turn: oncoming opposing traffic is held at a red light and you may turn left safely
questions.b: Yield to oncoming traffic before turning
questions.explanation: Protected green left arrow means oncoming cross traffic is halted, allowing safe left turns without oncoming conflicts.

questions.question: What does a Red Arrow traffic signal pointing left indicate?
questions.a: No left turn is permitted; vehicles intending to turn left must remain stopped behind the line even if circular signal is green
questions.c: Left lane is for emergency vehicles only
questions.explanation: A red arrow strictly prohibits turning in the direction of the arrow until the arrow turns green.

questions.question: What does a sign stating 'RIGHT TURN ON RED LIGHT WITH CAUTION' authorize drivers to do?
questions.a: Turn right on a red light after coming to a full stop, yielding to all cross traffic and pedestrians
questions.b: Turn right at 60 km/h without stopping
questions.c: Right turn is prohibited during red light
questions.explanation: Permits turning right on red only after a full stop and ensuring the maneuver will not impede oncoming priority traffic.

questions.question: In the absence of a 'Right Turn on Red' sign, is turning right on a red light legally permitted in the Philippines?
questions.a: Yes, anywhere in the country
questions.b: No, turning right on a steady red light is illegal unless specifically authorized by an explicit sign or green turn arrow
questions.explanation: Under standard traffic rules, red means stop. Right turn on red is prohibited unless a sign explicitly authorizes it.

questions.question: When an enforcer stands facing you with both arms outstretched horizontally, what does this hand signal indicate?
questions.a: Traffic approaching from the enforcer's front and rear must Stop completely
questions.b: Traffic may proceed at full speed
questions.explanation: Arms outstretched across your path signals a stop command to traffic approaching the enforcer's front and back.

questions.question: When a traffic enforcer stands sideways to your vehicle and motions with an underhand waving gesture toward themselves, what does it mean?
questions.a: Traffic in your direction is authorized to Proceed / Move forward
questions.explanation: The underhand beckoning wave authorizes traffic parallel to the enforcer's stance to proceed through the junction.

questions.question: What whistle signal does a Philippine traffic enforcer use to command traffic to STOP?
questions.a: One long, sharp blast of the whistle
questions.explanation: Standard police whistle code: One long sharp blast = STOP; Two short rapid blasts = GO / PROCEED.

questions.question: What whistle signal does a traffic enforcer use to command traffic to GO / PROCEED?
questions.a: Two short, sharp blasts of the whistle
questions.explanation: Two short blasts instruct stalled or waiting traffic to proceed forward.

questions.question: What does a Flashing Yellow Arrow signal pointing to the left mean?
questions.a: Unprotected left turn: you may turn left after yielding the right of way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
questions.explanation: Flashing yellow arrow indicates left turns are allowed, but you must yield to oncoming vehicles traveling straight.

questions.question: When a traffic light malfunctions (all lights are completely dark or flashing erratically), how should drivers treat the intersection?
questions.a: Speed through to clear the broken junction quickly
questions.b: Treat the intersection as an uncontrolled 4-way STOP junction, yielding to vehicles on the right and proceeding with extreme caution
questions.c: Wait for 1 hour until lights turn back on
questions.explanation: Dark traffic signals revert the junction to 4-way stop right-of-way rules where drivers must stop and yield before proceeding.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled 4-way intersection where two vehicles arrive at the exact same time from perpendicular roads, who has the right-of-way?
questions.a: Vehicle A (on the vertical road)
questions.b: Vehicle B on the right side of Vehicle A has the right-of-way
questions.explanation: Under RA 4136 Section 42(a), when two vehicles approach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the vehicle on their right.

questions.question: When making a Left Turn across opposing oncoming traffic at an intersection without a green turn arrow, you must:
questions.a: Speed up to turn before oncoming vehicles arrive
questions.b: Yield the right-of-way to all oncoming vehicles proceeding straight or turning right
questions.d: Flash your high beams to force oncoming traffic to stop
questions.explanation: Under Section 42(b) of RA 4136, a driver intending to turn left within an intersection must yield the right of way to any oncoming vehicle approaching straight or turning right.

questions.question: When an authorized Emergency Vehicle (Ambulance, Fire Truck, or Police Car) approaches sounding a siren or flashing red/blue lights, what must all drivers do?
questions.a: Speed up to clear the road ahead of the ambulance
questions.b: Immediately drive to the right-hand edge/curb of the road and come to a complete stop until it passes
questions.c: Stop immediately in the center lane
questions.d: Follow closely behind the emergency vehicle to bypass heavy traffic
questions.explanation: Under RA 4136 Section 43, drivers must immediately pull over as close as possible to the right-hand curb and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has completely passed.

questions.question: When entering a public highway or thoroughfare from a private driveway, garage, or building alley, who has the right-of-way?
questions.a: The vehicle exiting the private driveway
questions.b: All vehicles already traveling on the public highway
questions.c: The vehicle moving at the higher speed
questions.explanation: Under Section 42(c) of RA 4136, a driver entering a public highway from a private road or driveway must yield the right of way to all vehicles approaching on the highway.

questions.question: On a steep, narrow mountain road where two vehicles cannot pass each other simultaneously, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
questions.a: The vehicle descending (going downhill)
questions.explanation: The vehicle traveling uphill (ascending) has the right of way because it is harder to regain momentum and start from a standstill on a steep grade. The downhill vehicle must back up if needed.

questions.question: At a T-junction without traffic signs, which vehicle must yield the right-of-way?
questions.a: The vehicle traveling on the through road (top bar of the T)
questions.b: The vehicle traveling on the terminating road (stem of the T) must yield to through traffic
questions.explanation: Traffic on the terminating road must yield to vehicles flowing continuously along the through street.

questions.question: When two vehicles approach an uncontrolled intersection at different times, who has the right-of-way?
questions.a: The vehicle that reached and entered the intersection FIRST
questions.b: The vehicle that is traveling faster
questions.explanation: First-in, first-out rule: The driver of a vehicle who has already entered the intersection has right-of-way over vehicles still approaching.

questions.question: When turning right into a two-lane street with a pedestrian crossing the side street, who has right of way?
questions.a: The turning vehicle
questions.b: The pedestrian crossing the street has absolute right of way
questions.d: The vehicle if turning on green
questions.explanation: Pedestrians lawfully crossing within any marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection have right-of-way over turning vehicles.

questions.question: Does an official funeral procession or presidential motorcade accompanied by police escorts have right-of-way at intersections?
questions.a: No, they must follow normal red lights
questions.b: Yes, drivers must yield right-of-way and must not drive between vehicles of a lawful escort/procession
questions.explanation: Authorized motorcades and escorted processions have statutory priority; cutting into an escorted convoy is a traffic violation.

questions.question: When approaching a STOP sign at an intersection where another vehicle is stopped on the perpendicular street with a GIVE WAY sign, who proceeds first?
questions.a: The vehicle facing the GIVE WAY sign (once clear)
questions.b: The vehicle facing the STOP sign must make a full stop first; the vehicle on the priority road moves first
questions.explanation: A STOP sign mandates a full halt; drivers on priority streets or facing lesser yield signs have priority once the stop is made.

questions.question: If you are already inside an intersection waiting to complete a left turn when the traffic signal turns yellow and then red, what should you do?
questions.a: Reverse rapidly back behind the stop line
questions.b: Wait until oncoming traffic stops, then complete your left turn safely to clear the intersection
questions.c: Remain stopped directly in the center of the intersection
questions.explanation: Vehicles caught inside the junction to turn left should complete their turn once oncoming traffic halts to avoid gridlock.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an acceleration merge lane, do you have right-of-way over vehicles on the highway?
questions.a: Yes, merging traffic always has priority
questions.b: No, traffic on the main highway has right-of-way; merging vehicles must adjust speed and yield to open gaps
questions.c: Yes, if your turn signal is blinking
questions.d: Yes, if you drive faster than 100 km/h
questions.explanation: Highway through-traffic holds right-of-way; merging traffic must yield and merge seamlessly into gaps.

questions.question: At a four-way all-way stop intersection (4-Way STOP), if four vehicles arrive at the exact same instant from all 4 directions, how is right-of-way resolved safely?
questions.a: All drivers accelerate simultaneously
questions.b: Drivers yield to the right; if deadlocked, communication through hand gestures and eye contact establishes who proceeds first safely
questions.explanation: Mutual courtesy, eye contact, and yielding to the right resolve multi-vehicle deadlocks safely.

questions.question: What is the right-of-way rule between a motor vehicle and a train at an unprotected railway crossing?
questions.a: The motor vehicle has right of way if already on the tracks
questions.b: The train ALWAYS has absolute right-of-way because trains cannot stop quickly or swerve
questions.explanation: Trains always have absolute priority due to immense mass and stopping distances exceeding 500+ meters.

questions.question: When entering a traffic rotary (roundabout) with multiple lanes, when must you yield to bicycles in the circular roadway?
questions.a: Never, bicycles must yield to cars
questions.b: Always; bicycles inside the circulatory roadway are treated as vehicles and hold right-of-way
questions.c: Only if the bicycle has flashing lights
questions.explanation: Bicycles are legal vehicles on public roads and enjoy identical right-of-way protections in roundabouts.

questions.question: If an ambulance approaching from behind has its siren off but flashing emergency lights on, do you need to give way?
questions.a: No, only if the siren is sounding
questions.b: Yes, emergency lights alone signify an urgent emergency mission requiring all traffic to yield
questions.c: Only if it is a government ambulance
questions.explanation: Flashing emergency lights indicate an active emergency operation; drivers must yield right-of-way immediately.

questions.question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches from behind while you are stopped at a red traffic light with no room to pull right?
questions.a: Remain calm, wait until cross traffic is clear, then cautiously move forward or edge right into the intersection if safe to allow the emergency vehicle passage
questions.b: Reverse into the car behind you
questions.d: Get out of the car and run
questions.explanation: In gridlock at red lights, carefully inch forward or edge rightward safely to open a passage corridor.

questions.question: When leaving a designated parallel parking slot along the curb to enter traffic flow, who has right-of-way?
questions.a: The vehicle pulling out of the parking slot
questions.b: All moving vehicles already traveling in the traffic lane
questions.explanation: Vehicles departing from a parked position must wait and yield to all moving traffic in the lane.

questions.question: On a two-lane undivided road where one lane is obstructed by roadwork or a parked truck, which direction has right-of-way?
questions.a: The vehicle whose lane is obstructed must yield to oncoming traffic in the clear lane
questions.b: The vehicle with the obstruction has priority
questions.c: Whichever vehicle flashes high beams first
questions.explanation: The driver whose travel lane is physically blocked must wait until oncoming traffic in the unobstructed lane has cleared.

questions.question: What is the defensive driving philosophy regarding 'Right-of-Way'?
questions.a: Right-of-way is something you demand and take by force
questions.b: Right-of-way is something given by others to you, not something to be claimed aggressively at the expense of an avoidable crash
questions.c: Right-of-way belongs to whoever has the more expensive car
questions.d: Right-of-way is decided by vehicle weight
